decision_summary.portfolio_constraint_check: Primary lane L13; does not consume capped L03, L04, L06, or L14. Uses the portfolio's one remaining diagnostic_test slot.
decision_summary.critical_caveat: G4 is the dominant risk. Brookhaven already owns mature RHIC pC/HJET polarimeters and may implement the EIC cassette and readout in-house. The merchant wedge survives only if a continuously streaming, two-layer, self-calibrating cassette can beat the dead time and integration burden of CAEN-class rack digitizers and can earn a written EIC subsystem evaluation path by 2029.

candidate.concept: Deadtime-free 2 ns hadron-polarimeter recoil cassette for the Electron-Ion Collider: paired 12-strip silicon layers, 5 GS/s waveform front end, embedded Am/Gd calibration, and event-built optical readout
candidate.sector_cluster: Big-science accelerator polarimetry and beam diagnostics
named_buyer_examples: Brookhaven National Laboratory Electron-Ion Collider hadron-polarimetry work package
DOE Office of Nuclear Physics accelerator-diagnostics programs
Brookhaven RHIC polarimetry team as the legacy-system reference and likely EIC integrator
candidate.painful_job: EIC's approved requirements do not merely ask for generic polarization data: they require bunch-by-bunch pC polarization, 12-strip silicon recoil sensors, 25 keV energy resolution, waveform timing resolution of 0.5 ns or better, two silicon layers for punch-through rejection, and Am/Gd alpha calibration. DOE separately solicited bunch-by-bunch hadron polarimetry at bunch spacing as short as 2 ns. RHIC's proven pC/HJET instruments establish the physics but were built around much wider bunch spacing and bespoke lab electronics; a CAEN V1742 samples at 5 GS/s but imposes 110-181 microseconds of conversion dead time and is a rack digitizer rather than a calibrated detector cassette.
candidate.product: A vacuum-flange recoil telescope cassette containing two aligned twelve-strip silicon planes, low-capacitance dual-gain charge front ends, continuous 5 GS/s circular sampling, FPGA pulse extraction and time-of-flight/energy coincidence, remotely actuated Am-241 and Gd-148 calibration witnesses, bias-current and dose-health monitoring, and redundant optical event output. It reuses BNL's target mechanics and analyzing-power methods; it does not claim to replace the pC target, HJET, Breit-Rabi polarimeter, or facility timing system.
candidate.frontier_vision: Make collider-grade polarimetry a qualified instrumentation boundary instead of a one-off electronics project: the same recoil cassette can be regression-tested off-machine, swapped during a maintenance window, and reused for polarized proton and light-ion facilities without reopening the target or physics-analysis architecture.
candidate.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026: freeze the EIC requirement traceability matrix and characterize commercial silicon-strip capacitance, leakage, alpha response, and radiation drift. 2027: build two six-cassette electronics strings and demonstrate continuous dual-layer acquisition with synthetic 2 ns pulse pairs. 2028: complete an independently scheduled proton/carbon-recoil beam test under a paid facility-access agreement; no access is assumed in this proposal. 2029: integrate a non-beam vacuum mock-up with the published EIC interfaces and require a written BNL evaluation plan, paid qualification, CRADA, or procurement work package before counting commercial engagement.
candidate.launch_2030_timing_thesis: DOE's FY2026 construction justification funds EIC, records an official 1Q FY2036 project completion date, and the BNL CD-3B award authorizes additional long-lead procurement. The 2025 project review and detailed schedules extend integration activity through the first half of the 2030s. A 2030 launch therefore targets subsystem qualification, integration lots, commissioning spares, and radiation-life replacements during 2030-2035 rather than attempting to change the polarimetry physics after commissioning.
candidate.demand_trigger_2030_2035: EIC hadron-polarimeter fabrication, integration, commissioning, spares, and detector replacement work while the federally funded project moves from CD-3B procurement to its official 1Q FY2036 completion. The exact 2026 approved EIC requirements and DOE's explicit 2 ns polarimetry solicitation are the product specification; P5-USSCI-R03 and P5-USSCI-T03 are the independent project-timing bridges already proposed elsewhere in P5.
candidate.competition_outlook_2030: The closest substitute is BNL's in-house RHIC pC/HJET detector and DAQ lineage, which is scientifically proven and will be favored unless the merchant unit reduces integration risk. CAEN's V1742 already offers 32 channels, 12 bits, and 5 GS/s, but it has global triggered acquisition and 110-181 microseconds of conversion dead time. Teledyne e2v sells suitable multi-GS/s ADC silicon but not a polarimeter cassette. The functional wedge is continuous event extraction with no conversion stop, paired-layer coincidence, in-situ two-alpha calibration, bias/dose health, and a vacuum-ready replaceable cassette; it is not a new enclosure around a CAEN board.
candidate.g4_adverse_case: BNL may already have an unpublished or not-yet-frozen EIC readout that meets every listed metric, or may prefer an in-house board for configuration control. If so, there is no merchant whitespace. Do not select on the assumption that BNL must outsource.
candidate.timing_window_risk: The detector architecture could be frozen before the startup has a beam-qualified unit; EIC schedule changes could defer the procurement; or CAEN/BNL could remove dead time with an updated board. Kill by end-2028 if the target interface is frozen to a named in-house design with no second-source path, and kill commercially by end-2029 without a written evaluation or procurement route.
candidate.commercial_readiness_kill_date: 2034; earlier kill at end-2029 without a written EIC evaluation, paid qualification, CRADA, or procurement work package
candidate.extreme_edge: Separate recoil events from adjacent 2 ns bunches while preserving <=25 keV energy resolution and <=0.5 ns waveform timing, with zero acquisition-stop dead time and continuous calibration drift records.
candidate.first_experiment: Nine-month 2027-2028 qualification: build six paired 12-strip silicon cassettes and a 144-channel continuous-sampling readout. Use Am-241/Gd-148 sources, programmable double-pulse charge injection, and a separately contracted proton/carbon-recoil beam test. Pass only if every active strip achieves <=25 keV FWHM-equivalent energy resolution over the specified recoil range, <=0.5 ns RMS timing, >=95% correct separation of equal-amplitude pulses 2 ns apart, >=99% punch-through/background rejection from the second layer, <0.2% gain drift after auto-calibration, no global conversion dead time at 100,000 accepted events/s, and no silent event loss under 24-hour fault injection. Kill on failure of any load-bearing metric, on >5% dead channels after dose testing, or if two independent EIC detector engineers reject the mechanical/data interface.
candidate.design_in_or_procurement_engagement_path: A written BNL interface evaluation followed by a paid qualification, CRADA, approved second-source plan, or polarimetry work package. A scientific conversation without one of these artifacts does not count.
candidate.safety_regulatory_export_path: US DOE civilian science is the base case. The cassette uses sealed calibration sources only under licensed institutional procedures; the startup may instead supply source-compatible mechanics while BNL owns the sources. Design controls cover high-voltage bias, vacuum materials, radiation activation, interlocks, source shutters, configuration control, cybersecurity of optical readout, domestic sourcing, and export classification before any non-US quotation.
candidate.founder_fit_note: The core transfer is mixed-signal electronics, FPGA streaming, sensor calibration, controls, and automated qualification. Polarized-beam physics, silicon-detector packaging, sealed-source licensing, and DOE configuration control require specialist partners.

G1.rationale: DOE's FY25 buyer solicitation explicitly requests bunch-by-bunch hadron polarimetry at 2 ns, while EIC's approved 2026 buyer requirements specify the exact silicon layers, strip geometry, timing, energy resolution, alpha calibration, and bunch-by-bunch job. BNL CD-3B and DOE FY26 funding independently establish an active funded buyer program.

G2.rationale: Seven final journal/proceedings works have DOI or stable publisher records and explicit final-venue evidence; no preprint is counted.

G3.rationale: The $185k experiment has six paired cassettes, exact energy/timing/double-pulse/background/drift/dead-time/dose metrics, independent beam-test contracting, and hard technical and buyer-interface kills.

G4.rationale: BNL's in-house RHIC system and CAEN V1742 are named adverse incumbents. The architecture difference is continuous event extraction plus two-layer coincidence, embedded dual-alpha calibration, dose/bias health, and replaceable vacuum cassette. The pass is marginal because BNL may already be converging on an equivalent in-house EIC board.

G5.rationale: Silicon recoil detection, HJET/pC physics, sub-nanosecond waveform acquisition, and multi-GHz event electronics are individually demonstrated. The bounded experiment directly tests the remaining high-rate integration risk.

G6.rationale: US-only DOE civilian deployment, sealed-source institutional custody, radiation/high-voltage/vacuum interlocks, configuration control, cybersecurity, domestic sourcing, and export screening are explicit.

G7.rationale: The 2026-2029 path, TRL 3-to-7 plan, exact 2026 requirements, CD-3B procurement, official DOE project completion in 1Q FY2036, 2030-2035 integration/spares use, incumbent risk, and 2028/2029/2034 kill dates are explicit. P5-USSCI-R03 supplies an independent project-review timing bridge.

candidate.distinctness_check: Not a detector timing-distribution endpoint, SRF LLRF/piezo controller, or a relabel of D16/A05/D19/A02/A21/A22. The product's necessary job is hadron-polarimeter recoil acquisition and calibration.
